mathematical_lesson: Coarse high-half occupancy is not sufficient for exact backward coupling: the fresh-row label map must also be congruent with the canonical prefix language.

proof_steps.derivation: Fix n>=18 and M=2^(n-1). In MIRROR_ONLY the level-n complement is the inherited old-old copy of U_(n-1) together with new-old cells (M+r,c) selected by the unchanged decoder on bin_(n-1)(r)||bin_(n-1)(c). TWO_SIDED adds only old-new cells (r,M+c) selected by that same predicate. Neither variant adds new-new cells, changes labels, or places suffix c on the fresh row.

Every inherited old-old cell and every optional old-new cell has row r<M, so its n-bit row label begins 0. A new-old cell has row M+r, whose n-bit label is 1 concatenated with bin_(n-1)(r). These exhaustive clauses reduce the high-row classification to the decoded word that selected the new-old cell.

The unchanged total decoder has exactly three output routes relevant here: the all-zero word decodes to the fixed contradiction; a well-formed word starting MAGIC=11100101 decodes to its canonical formula; every other word decodes to a tautology. Hence an UNSAT selecting word is either all-zero, giving r=0 and fresh-row label 1 followed by n-1 zeros, or a valid MAGIC word. Since n-1>=17>8, the latter has bin_(n-1)(r) beginning with the full MAGIC header and its fresh-row label begins 1||MAGIC.

Every current canonical n-bit prefix begins MAGIC=11100101. A low inherited/old-new row begins 0 and differs at bit 1. The all-zero fresh row begins 10 and differs from MAGIC=11... at bit 2. A canonical mirror row begins 1||MAGIC, whose first four bits are 1111, whereas MAGIC has first four bits 1110; these differ at bit 4. Thus none of the three exhaustive row classes equals a current canonical prefix.

P2-P4 apply to MIRROR_ONLY. TWO_SIDED adds only old-new complement cells whose rows remain below M and are already covered by the low-row case. Therefore for every n>=18 both variants have complement row projection disjoint from all current canonical MAGIC n-bit prefixes. In particular no current canonical UNSAT prefix row collides.
